facts_summary: The Assessing Officer disallowed interest expenses amounting to INR 4.50 Cr under Rule 8D(2)(ii) read with Section 14A, alleging that borrowed funds were utilized in strategic equity investments in subsidiaries yielding exempt dividend income. The company maintains that its paid-up share capital and free reserves (INR 320 Cr) substantially exceed the total tax-free equity investments (INR 42 Cr), and no borrowed funds were specifically deployed.
department_arguments: Investments were made from a common treasury pool where loan funds and equity funds are intermingled. Rule 8D is mandatory once expenditure is incurred in relation to exempt income, regardless of the company's internal fund allocation claims.
company_arguments: Under the Supreme Court ruling in South Indian Bank (2021) and Bombay HC in Reliance Utilities, where interest-free owned surplus funds exceed tax-free investments, statutory presumption applies that investments were made out of own funds. Further, during FY 2019-20, exempt dividend earned was only INR 12 Lakhs.
status: Pending before ITAT Mumbai Bench. Company paid 20% pre-deposit under protest for stay of demand.

company_name: Nova Cloud Systems India Pvt Ltd
dispute_type: Transfer Pricing - AMP Expenditure & Marketing Intangibles
facts_summary: The Transfer Pricing Officer (TPO) made an upward TP adjustment of INR 12.50 Cr by applying the Bright Line Test (BLT) on Advertising, Marketing and Promotion (AMP) expenses incurred in India. The TPO alleged that Nova India spent 8.5% of sales on AMP compared to domestic peer average of 2.1%, thereby building brand equity for its US parent entity without receiving arm's length compensation.
department_arguments: Excessive AMP expenditure constitutes an international transaction of brand building for the foreign trademark owner, requiring markup and reimbursement under Section 92B.
company_arguments: Nova India operates as a full-fledged distributor and bears entrepreneurial risks. Under Delhi High Court landmark rulings in Sony Ericsson (2015) and Maruti Suzuki (2016), the Bright Line Test is legally non-existent under the Indian IT Act. In the absence of an express agreement with the foreign AE, domestic marketing spend cannot be characterized as an international transaction.
status: Final assessment order issued u/s 143(3) r.w.s. 144C; appeal pending before ITAT Delhi.

dispute_type: Input Tax Credit (ITC) Denial u/s 16(2)(c) - Supplier Default
facts_summary: The GST Department issued an order u/s 73 demanding reversal of ITC of INR 2.80 Cr along with interest u/s 50 and penalty, on the ground that two key logistics and warehousing vendors did not reflect the invoices in their GSTR-1, or had their GST registrations cancelled retrospectively due to non-payment of taxes.
department_arguments: Under Section 16(2)(c) of the CGST Act, entitlement to ITC is contingent upon tax actually being deposited into the government treasury by the supplier. Unpaid invoices cannot generate valid input credit.
company_arguments: Zenith possesses genuine e-way bills, tax invoices, and proof of electronic bank payments. Under Calcutta HC in Suncraft Energy (2023) and Madras HC in D.Y. Beathel, the Department cannot summarily reverse recipient's ITC without first initiating statutory recovery against the defaulting vendors. Circular 183 also supports bona fide claims.
status: Appeal filed u/s 107 with 10% statutory pre-deposit of INR 28 Lakhs.

dispute_type: Delayed Employee Contribution to PF/ESI u/s 36(1)(va)
facts_summary: CPC Bengaluru made a prima facie adjustment u/s 143(1)(a) disallowing INR 1.85 Cr of employee contributions to provident fund and ESI on the grounds that the funds were deposited between 2 to 5 days after the 15th of the subsequent month (the statutory due date under the PF Act), but well before the due date for filing return of income u/s 139(1).
department_arguments: Supreme Court in Checkmate Services (October 2022) conclusively held that Section 43B does not cover employee contributions. Delayed deposit beyond the statutory labor law deadline results in permanent disallowance.
company_arguments: The company argued reasonable cause due to banking gateway downtime during COVID-19 lockdown, and that deposits were made prior to the return filing date under historical Karnataka High Court precedents.
status: Pending before CIT(A). Very high risk of crystallizing into a permanent cash liability in light of the Supreme Court ruling.
